messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point

message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (≈ 0.1 atm) water’s freezing point drops to roughly **–2 °C**.  
This is consistent with the water‑phase diagram: at 10 kPa the solid–liquid equilibrium line lies just below the triple‑point temperature (≈ 0.01 °C at 61.16 kPa). Thus, under 10 kPa, pure water will freeze at about –2 °C before it can exist as a liquid.
